newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Widow of Israel's Rabin says his death "wasted".
newsitem.headline: Widow of Israel's Rabin says his death "wasted".

text.p: The widow of assassinated Israeli Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin said on Thursday that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's landmark handshake with the PLO's Yasser Arafat made her husband's murder a "worthless sacrifice."

"More than any other day since the murder I can perhaps feel I am sorry for him (Rabin) and for his sacrifice. More than any other day yesterday he seemed like a wasted sacrifice, a worthless sacrifice," Leah Rabin told Israel's army radio.
"Why did they kill him? For the path he created -- that he came to realise in the end there was no other way, no alternative to it," she said.

Yitzhak Rabin was gunned down at a peace rally last November by a right-wing religious Jew opposed to peace deals Rabin had signed with the PLO handing over parts of the West Bank and Gaza Strip to Palestinian self-rule.
Leah Rabin accused Netanyahu at the time of fostering a climate of hatred which led to the assassination. As opposition leader Netanyahu had condemned the peace deals.
Rabin sealed his peace accord on the White House lawn in Washington in September 1993 by shaking the hand of Arafat, leader of the Palestine Liberation Organisation.
Netanyahu, who ousted Rabin's successor Shimon Peres in May elections, said while campaigning that he would never meet the Palestinian leader.
Netanyahu, 46, met Arafat, 67, for the first time on Wednesday, relaunching stalled talks on extending self-rule.
